transcript.text: Bosch KGN34NL3AG - some days it's fine, other days it just clicks every few minutes at the back and doesn't seem to run, and the freezer starts getting soft. Then it starts working again by itself. What's going on?

For safety, please switch the fridge freezer off at the socket and unplug it first. Do not open, bend or pierce any of the pipes or the cooling circuit as it is sealed and needs a refrigeration engineer. Clicking without starting can happen when it overheats. Gently dust or vacuum the coil or grille at the back or underneath, and leave a few centimetres of space round it, then give it a couple of hours. Was it dusty or pushed against the wall (and have you sorted it), or was it already clean with space?
Thank you. The back was a bit dusty, but there is a gap between the fridge and the wall. I haven't cleaned it yet, so I can do that. Should I leave it unplugged for a while afterwards?

Thanks for checking that. Since you found it blocked, clearing it is the next step and may well sort the issue. Clicking without starting can happen when the unit overheats. Please switch the fridge freezer off at the socket and unplug it first. Do not open, bend or pierce any of the pipes or the cooling circuit as it is sealed and needs a refrigeration engineer. Gently dust or vacuum the coil or grille at the back or underneath, and leave a few centimetres of space round it, then give it a couple of hours. Was it dusty or pushed against the wall (and have you sorted it), or was it already clean with space?

As I said, the back was a bit dusty but there is a gap between the fridge and the wall, and I haven't cleaned it yet. I'll unplug it and vacuum the back now. There has been no burning smell and nothing has tripped. Do I need to leave it unplugged for a while afterwards, and is there anything else I should check?

[Heading: Compressor start device / compressor]
Clicking every few minutes without starting suggests the compressor is trying to start but its protector cuts it out, likely due to the start device or the compressor itself. I am not recommending any specific part from here. Meanwhile, keep the doors shut: a full freezer typically stays frozen for about a day if left unopened. Chilled food warmer than 8°C for over four hours is safest thrown away, and thawed food should not be refrozen unless cooked first. Switch the fridge freezer off at the socket and unplug it first. Do not open, bend or pierce any of the pipes or the cooling circuit as it is sealed and needs a refrigeration engineer. If you haven't had a chance yet, the check I described earlier comes first.
